title: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) block structure
summary: AES is a symmetric block cipher with a 128-bit block size and key sizes of 128, 192, or 256 bits. A 128-bit block is a 4x4 matrix of bytes (state). Encryption: initial AddRoundKey, then (Nr-1) rounds of SubBytes (S-box), ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey, then a final round without MixColumns. Nr = 10 (128-bit key), 12 (192-bit), or 14 (256-bit).

structure.meaning: 4x4 matrix of bytes, column-major order. Input plaintext block.
Each byte replaced by S-box lookup (non-linear substitution, 256-entry table).
Row i shifted left by i bytes (row 0: 0, row 1: 1, row 2: 2, row 3: 3).
Each column multiplied by a fixed 4x4 matrix over GF(2^8) (polynomial 0x11B).
XOR state with the round key (128 bits, derived by key schedule).
Expands the cipher key into (Nr+1) round keys using RotWord, SubWord (S-box), and Rcon (round constant).

ext.example_decoded: AES input block (plaintext) in column-major order
notes: AES operates on 128-bit (16-byte) blocks regardless of key size.
Modes of operation: ECB (insecure, don't use), CBC, CTR, GCM (authenticated), CCM.
AES-NI instructions (Intel/AMD) accelerate SubBytes and MixColumns.
GCM (Galois/Counter Mode) is the most common authenticated encryption mode (TLS, IPsec, etc.).
AES-256 is quantum-resistant (Grover's algorithm halves the effective key length to 128 bits).
